research_question: Did the gap in within-cohort math achievement percentile rank between lowest-band and highest-band SES students change between the ELS:2002 and HSLS:09 cohorts, and how much of any raw change is accounted for by compositional shift within the SES bands versus a change at fixed composition (composition-adjusted gap-in-gaps with ML heterogeneity)?

outcome.definition: within-cohort percentile rank (0-100) of the base-wave standardized math score

rationale_for_method_set: M9 (within-group AIPW cohort standardization; certified bias 0.0003, coverage 1.0) answers the composition-fixed question; M8 raw is the always-reported comparator whose contrast with M9 is the substantive story; M10 (certified contrast-based) mines heterogeneity with boosted outcome models.
known_concerns_to_flag: CCD-01 non-equated tests: only rank-gap changes are estimable
CCD-02 bundled treatment: the 2002-2009 cohort contrast bundles many changes; no single-policy attribution
grade offset: ELS base wave is grade 10, HSLS base wave is grade 9
harmonization coarseness: HSLS parent-education lacks a some-college-no-degree category
pared3 is a component of the SES composite: it enters only as WITHIN-GROUP cohort-composition adjustment, never as a cross-group control
